summary: IDS feed s168_triple is degraded with 3 faults: 41.7% one-way TCP sessions (IDS requires bidirectional), 73.6% encrypted bytes exceeding 60% tolerance, and 1.57 Gbps microbursts overloading 1 Gbps IDS port (157% capacity). Detection coverage is significantly reduced.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one direction for many flows - 85 of 204 TCP sessions (41.7%) are unidirectional. Likely asymmetric routing with single-leg capture or broker not aggregating both directions of the conversation to the same tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP stream reassembly, handshake tracking, and stateful signatures. With only one side, it cannot reconstruct sessions, misses client-to-server attacks and server responses, and generates false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port so the IDS sees complete sessions for stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic microbursts peak at 1.57 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (157% overload, 6 overloaded intervals). Packet broker is sending line-rate bursts without shaping or distribution.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port overrun causes indiscriminate packet drops at the tool NIC. IDS will miss exploits during bursts, lose flow state, and have incomplete forensic capture exactly when traffic is highest.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across 2+ IDS ports or add load-balancing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops while preserving full payload to IDS.

findings.root_cause: 74% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is predominantly encrypted without prior decryption on the visibility fabric.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for signature and anomaly detection. With 73.6% encrypted, payload inspection is blind for most traffic, drastically reducing detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS sessions upstream (or selectively forward cleartext via SSL visibility appliance) so IDS receives inspectable payload within its tolerance.
